intro: Convert gigabytes (GB) into terabytes (TB) accurately for NVMe SSDs, external hard drives, NAS arrays, and cloud storage quotas. Under the international SI decimal standard (IEC/NIST), 1,000 GB in 1 TB means 1 gigabyte equals 0.001 terabytes—simply divide gigabytes by 1,000. Compare decimal capacity against binary operating-system sizes and scan common drive tiers from 1 GB to 10,000 GB below.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: SI Decimal (1 TB = 1,000 GB) vs. Binary OS Reporting (1 TiB = 1,024 GiB)
items: Hard drive, SSD, and cloud vendors define 1 TB using base-10 SI prefixes (1,000 GB = 10¹² bytes), whereas Windows calculates capacity in binary powers of 1,024 (1 TiB = 1,024 GiB) while displaying 'TB' or 'GB'—making a 1 TB drive appear as roughly 931 GB (0.909 TiB).
Moving one step higher on the decimal storage scale, 1 petabyte (PB) equals 1,000 TB or 1,000,000 GB.

faqs.question: How many GB are in a TB?
faqs.answer: There are 1,000 gigabytes (GB) in 1 decimal terabyte (TB) under the international SI standard used by drive manufacturers and cloud providers. In binary computing (tebibytes), 1 TiB equals 1,024 GiB.

faqs.question: How do I convert gigabytes to terabytes?
faqs.answer: Divide the number of gigabytes by 1,000 (or multiply by 0.001): TB = GB ÷ 1,000. For example, 500 GB ÷ 1,000 = 0.5 TB.

faqs.question: What is 100 GB in TB?
faqs.answer: 100 gigabytes equals 0.1 terabytes (100 ÷ 1,000 = 0.1 TB) using the SI decimal storage standard.

faqs.question: Why does a 1 TB hard drive show around 931 GB in Windows?
faqs.answer: Manufacturers label 1 TB as 1,000,000,000,000 bytes (1,000 GB), whereas Windows divides bytes by 1,024³ (binary gibibytes) while still displaying 'GB': 10¹² ÷ 1,073,741,824 ≈ 931.32 GiB.
